# onl-bench

Speed + LIBERO success benchmarks for VLA policies. One run → one JSON row in `results/`.

## Latest results

<!-- results:start (generated by scripts/update_readme.py) -->
- **Success:** π0.5 98–100%, SmolVLA 75–78%.
- **Compile (`compile_autotune` vs `native` p50):** π0.5 286 → 59 ms (4.8× speed, 624 s one-time compile, success 100% → 100%); SmolVLA 273 → 33 ms (8.3× speed, 738 s one-time compile, success 75% → 77%).
- **Precision (fp32, fp16 no faster than native):** π0.5 native 286, fp32 381, fp16 343 ms; SmolVLA native 273, fp32 279, fp16 608 ms.

## Run it

```bash
# full row (speed + 100-episode LIBERO-Object success eval, ~$1 of GPU)
modal run modal_app.py::main --model smolvla --technique native

# cheap speed-only smoke (skips the paid eval)
modal run modal_app.py::main --model smolvla --technique native --episodes-per-task 0

# per-stage latency breakdown across techniques (speed only, no eval)
modal run modal_app.py::breakdown_main --techniques native,fp32,fp16,compile,compile_autotune

# a long run that must outlive this terminal; the row is saved to the Volume
modal run --detach modal_app.py::main --model pi05 --technique fp32
```

Needs a Modal secret `huggingface` holding `HF_TOKEN`, from an account that has accepted
the license of [google/paligemma-3b-pt-224](https://huggingface.co/google/paligemma-3b-pt-224)
(pi05's gated tokenizer).

Techniques set how the policy computes: `native` runs as the checkpoint ships (bf16 for
the SmolVLA LIBERO checkpoint), `fp32` casts the weights with `policy.to(float32)`, and
`fp16` uses `torch.autocast(float16)` over the native weights, because a weight cast
crashes SmolVLA. `compile` is
`native` plus `torch.compile` (`compile_model=true`) in torch's `default` mode;
`compile_autotune` is the same in `max-autotune`, lerobot's default.

**A row is either fully compiled or fully uncompiled.** The technique sets
`compile_model` in both the speed path and the eval, overriding the checkpoint: pi05
stores `true`, yet its `native`, `fp32` and `fp16` rows run uncompiled. A policy that
does not match its label stops the run.

`compile_s` is the wall time of the first call in the speed path (batch 1), including one
ordinary step, and is null on uncompiled rows. The eval compiles again at its own batch
size, which `compile_s` does not cover.

## Layout

| file | role |
|------|------|
| `bench/models.py` | model registry — adding a model is one `ModelSpec` entry |
| `bench/techniques.py` | precision techniques (autocast dtype per technique) |
| `bench/policy.py` | load policy + build synthetic observation (from dpc-two) |
| `bench/profiler.py` | step timing: batch 1, 10 warmup + 200 timed |
| `bench/speed.py` | run the speed benchmark under one technique |
| `bench/success.py` | run the LIBERO eval, read `eval_info.json` |
| `bench/_eval_entry.py` | wrapper that drives lerobot-eval precision per technique |
| `bench/row.py` | build + validate + write the 21-field result row |
| `modal_app.py` | Modal app + `modal run` entrypoint |
| `board/app.py` | the leaderboard Space; reads `results/*.json` and `CLAUDE.md` |
| `scripts/update_readme.py` | regenerates the README's results section |
| `docs/workflows.md` | terminology, concepts and workflows behind the results |

## One GPU

Speed is only comparable on one card, so every row is pinned to **L40S** and a run that
lands on anything else stops before measuring. Modal's `A10` served both an `NVIDIA A10`
and an `NVIDIA A10G` with no way to choose, about 27% apart on the same pi05 work.

Success does not depend on the card. `scripts/merge_speed_rows.py` keeps the success
fields of rows evaluated before the pin and takes everything else from a speed-only L40S
run. So `gpu` and `git_sha` say where a row's speed came from, and `success_gpu` and
`success_git_sha` say where its success came from.

## Precision & lerobot-eval

`lerobot-eval` has no CLI lever that casts SmolVLA's weights: `--policy.dtype` is
a no-op for SmolVLA, and `--policy.use_amp` only toggles autocast (a near no-op on
already-bf16 weights). So `_eval_entry` patches the eval module's `make_policy` to
`policy.to(dtype)` right after the policy is built, then runs the official eval
loop unchanged (`native` runs it with no patch). It asserts the cast took, so a
run can't silently report the wrong precision — matching how the speed path casts.

pi05 caches its build-time precision and picks its vision autocast from it, so
`cast_weights` updates that too. Its `fp16` row is only fp16 outside the vision tower: the
policy's own nested bf16 autocast wins inside it.

`denoise_steps` and `n_action_steps` are recorded in every row because they drive speed.
`p50_ms`/`hz` time one full chunk generation, so one model's `hz` is a control rate only
when `n_action_steps` is 1. pi05 runs at `n_action_steps=10` (the checkpoint stores 50),
as LeRobot's published LIBERO scores do.

`--eval.n_episodes` is **per task**; LIBERO-Object has 10 tasks, so
`--episodes-per-task 10` → 100 total episodes (seed 1000), per CLAUDE.md.

## Dev

```bash
uv sync
uv run ruff check .
uv run pytest        # GPU-free plumbing tests
```

## Leaderboard

```bash
uv run python board/app.py   # http://127.0.0.1:7860
```

The front matter at the top of this file configures the Hugging Face Space. Publish or
update it with this one command, which sends only the files the Space needs and drops rows
no longer in `results/`:

```bash
hf upload basithcodes/onl-bench-leaderboard . . --repo-type space \
  --include README.md --include requirements.txt --include CLAUDE.md \
  --include board/app.py --include "results/*.json" --delete "results/*.json"
```

After new rows, refresh the results section with `uv run python scripts/update_readme.py`;
a test fails until you do. `sdk_version` above and the pin in `requirements.txt` must match the locked versions; a test
checks this.
